data.text: Playwright enables reliable end-to-end testing across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API.

data.title: Playwright test

data.text: Playwright is a browser automation library whose test runner supports Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through the same API. That means a test written once can be run against all three, which catches engine-specific bugs that a single-browser suite misses. It also has built-in tracing.

data.title: A test across a browser matrix

data.text: Locators auto-wait until the element is actionable, so an explicit sleep is almost never needed. Fixtures such as `page` and `request` are injected into each test and can be extended for logged-in state. When a test fails, the trace viewer records a DOM snapshot of each step so you can replay it.

data.title: A reusable logged-in fixture
Interview angle: Cypress vs Playwright
data.text: Both drive a real browser. The practical differences are that Playwright runs the same suite across three engines, runs tests in parallel out of the box, and has first-class support for multiple tabs and contexts — where Cypress historically specialized in an interactive developer experience. Pick based on whether cross-browser coverage or the in-browser debugging flow matters more, and name that trade-off.
